text: Sunday morning I woke up feeling fresh and wrote up this week's DJ set on my blog. I like to break the post into numbered items.
For lunch I went to the burrito place across from the office and ordered my usual again.
Late tonight I worked on a DJ mix. Building it around heavily repetitive tracks made the flow feel right.
Stayed late at work and was wiped out, so I picked up the same chicken rice bowl from my regular shop that I always get.
On a rainy morning I tried the new seasonal drink at a cafe. The quiet corner seat made it easy to focus.
My manager asked me to take on a new project but the schedule looked too tight and it made me anxious.
I put only three items on tomorrow's to-do list. When I am tired a long list just makes me avoid it.
I went with my friend Jay to a ramen place neither of us had tried. Trying somewhere new was exciting.
On Saturday at the library I wrote a short work memo. I put the conclusion first and kept the reasoning to two lines.
Practiced my DJ set tonight. When it rains I pick calmer tracks.
Felt fresh this morning, so I ran in the park. It was my first ever 10 km.
Lunch again at the burrito place I always go to.
I was tired but tried a new gym with a free trial pass anyway.
While drafting a blog post my sentences got long, so I split them in two. I find an informational format easiest to write.
Jay listened to my DJ set and said he loved the heavily repetitive tracks.
A bright clear morning and I felt great, so I visited two new cafes.
On Sunday evening I planned the week in my to-do app, the same way I always do.
I was exhausted so lunch was the same convenience-store sandwich I always buy.
After feedback from my manager I replied by email and kept it short: a greeting, the key point, then my request.
After a late night at work I was too tired for DJ practice, so I went to bed early.
At lunch I tried a Vietnamese noodle shop for the first time because a teammate recommended it.
On a rainy night I finished a mix with calm tracks.
On Saturday morning I published my blog post as a numbered list, as usual, focused on information.
Tired on a Sunday evening, I ordered delivery from my usual fried chicken place, the same order as always.
It is the end of the month and my budget is tight, so I cooked dinner at home.
A fresh morning on my commute, so I listened to a brand new playlist.
Lunch was at my usual spot near the office, as usual.
I wrote only three things on my to-do list. It is my habit on tired days.
Went to our regular izakaya with Jay again.
In code review I blocked a pull request because it had no tests, even though the change itself was small.
I asked a teammate to split a huge pull request into smaller ones. I review small changes much faster.
The deadline moved up a week. I cut scope instead of cutting quality and told the team early.
When learning the new framework I wanted a working example before reading the rules, so I built a tiny project first.
I wanted a new keyboard but waited a week and compared three options before buying anything.
On the trip to Lisbon I skipped the tourist spots and walked through neighborhoods all day.
I asked an AI assistant for a summary and told it to keep answers short and stop asking me clarifying questions.
Asked the AI to include sources whenever it states a fact, since I double-check everything.
A one on one with my manager got tense, so I asked for the feedback in writing to think it over.
I decided quickly on the vendor, then revisited the choice two days later with fresh eyes.
When I am tired I pick the familiar option, and when I feel energetic I try something new.
